name: Input
description: Collects single-line text, with search mode offering a clear button and live result count.

constraints: Use for format hints only, not as a replacement for labels

type.description: Native input type. search adds a leading glyph, a clear button, Escape to clear then leave, and the count slot

size.description: Field height on the shared control track: 24, 28, 32 or 40

invalid.description: The danger edge and aria-invalid; say why in a Field.Error. Inside a Field, the Field's invalid does the same

disabled.description: Dims the field and blocks input

readOnly.description: Shows the value on a dashed edge without letting it change

startAdornment.description: Content before the text: a glyph or a prefix

endAdornment.description: Content after the text: a glyph, a suffix or an action

shortcut.description: A keyboard shortcut hint drawn at the end. Display only: the app owns the shortcut

count.description: type="search" only: how many match ("3 of 40"), announced politely while there is a query

onValueChange.description: Called with the new value on every change, the clear button and Escape included

when: Single-line answers: name, email, password, phone, URL
Filtering a list or a ledger as the person types (type="search")
Short free-form values a list cannot cover
whenNot: Numbers people step or scrub (use NumberField)
Selecting from predefined options (use Select or Combobox)
guidelines: Wrap in a Field for the label, description and error
Match type to the data: it drives validation and mobile keyboards
Placeholder shows format; it never replaces the label
Set invalid with a Field.Error that says why
A search field takes count while it filters; Escape clears, then leaves the field
shortcut is a hint only; register the key in the app
accessibility: Field.Label names the input and Field.Description describes it
Field.Error is announced when it appears
The clear button is named Clear and keeps focus in the field
The search count is a polite status, silent while the query is empty

examples.name: Default
examples.description: A Field gives the input its label.

examples.name: With description
examples.description: Supporting text sits under the field and describes it.

examples.name: Invalid
examples.description: The danger edge with the reason under the field.
examples.code:
<Field invalid>
  <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
  <Input type="email" defaultValue="invalid-email" />
  <Field.Error match>Enter a valid email address.</Field.Error>
</Field>

examples.name: Search
examples.description: A filter with a clear button, Escape to clear and a live count.
examples.code:
<Input
  type="search"
  aria-label="Filter components"
  placeholder="Filter"
  count="3 of 71"
  shortcut="/"
/>

examples.name: Read only
examples.description: A dashed edge: the value can be read and copied, not changed.

examples.name: Sizes
examples.description: Four heights on the control track: 24, 28, 32, 40.
examples.code:
<Stack gap="sm">
  <Input aria-label="Extra small" size="xs" />
  <Input aria-label="Small" size="sm" />
  <Input aria-label="Medium" size="md" />
  <Input aria-label="Large" size="lg" />
</Stack>

examples.name: Adornments
examples.description: A prefix and a suffix inside the field.

relations.note: Field supplies the label, description and error
Use NumberField for numbers people step or scrub
Use Select when choosing from predefined options

propsSummary: invalid: boolean - danger edge plus aria-invalid; pair with Field.Error
count: string - search match count, a polite status
shortcut: string - display-only kbd hint; do not hand-roll kbd markup
onValueChange: (value: string) => void; onChange stays the native event
Label, description and error come from Field parts, never from Input props
...native input attributes are supported (autoComplete, required, inputMode, pattern, etc.)
